column1: # Xenoblade Chronicles 2 on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Monolith Soft's engine on SDK 3.5.0, update 2.1.0 (v983040); 12,750 shaders in the bundle (base game, update and the New Quests Pack; the other DLC's shaders are not in it).
# Tested 2026-11-14 on the AYN Odin 3 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 15), Turnip (Mesa 26.99, Banners-Turnip v27.0.0-20261114-r4 A8xx) and Qualcomm's 512.800.72:
# boot, the title, a new game, the King Crustip tutorial fight and the first steps in Argentum. 60 fps through patches.py's frame step (30 in cutscenes; DM_FPS_TARGET=30
# in env.txt for 30 everywhere). In the fight at 896x504 (DM_RENDER_SCALE=0.5), frames p95 / GPU p50 / submit+present p50: Qualcomm 19.4 / 8.1 / 7.7 ms, Turnip 16.9 / 6.9 / 4.3 ms,
# Turnip with the replay on its own thread (the env rows below) 16.8 / 6.9 / 2.3 ms. One run each, no red lines. At 60 fps and 1280x720 the SoC reached 101-104 C.
# 2026-11-15, Turnip: sound (the SDK 3.5.0 renderer layout, hle_audren.c), the movies (the two-argument movie::Decoder, hle_movie.c), the game's own save made and loaded,
# a fight and Argentum at 1280x720 and 60 fps (frames p95 16.9-17.6 ms, GPU about 10 ms with the two depth rows below).
# DM_VK_FDZ=0, DM_VK_LRZ_TOUCH=0: the host's depth workarounds for Qualcomm's driver (gfx_vk_exec.c: the fragment-depth variants, the LRZ touch) cost GPU time here and
# the picture is the same without them on Turnip (the title scene at 1280x720: the fragment-depth variants alone took the deferred lighting pass from 0.20 to 1.99 ms and
# the frame from 10.0 to 12.0 ms of GPU). Checked on Turnip only: on Qualcomm's driver the game was run with both on (2026-11-14), not with these rows.
# Open: later areas, long sessions, the DLC; one crash on losing focus in Argentum, not reproduced.
